pages.text: "I can carry it!" Lolo grabbed a basin of sardines. The ground in front of Mom's stall was slippery. Yellow boots slid forward.
Splash—the water spilled, and sardines scattered across the ground. "Oh... what do I do?" Lolo froze. The market bustled; farther away, Mom handed a customer a parcel.
Lolo quietly pushed the empty basin behind a box and nudged the sardines underneath with a foot. Then Lolo put both hands behind their back, pretending nothing had happened.
But Lolo's heart kept thumping. Lolo kept looking back, afraid Mom would come over. Even Riri's invitation to play did not register.
Riri looked behind the box. "Lolo, did you spill this?" Lolo lowered their head. "I was afraid of being scolded..." "Spilled it? Tell Mom!" Riri held Lolo's hand.
"Mom will be more upset about hiding it than spilling it." Looking down at their toes, Lolo took a deep breath. "...Will you come with me?" Riri squeezed Lolo's hand tighter.
Lolo stood in front of Mom's blue apron. "Mom, I spilled the basin. I hid it behind the box. I am sorry." The voice was very quiet, but Lolo said everything.
Mom did not get angry. "Thank you for telling me." Lolo's thumping heart felt light again. All three crouched to pick up sardines. Mom poured seawater over them to rinse them.
The basin was full of clean sardines again. "One, stop where you are if you spill! Two, tell a grown-up right away! Three, clean up together!" This time, Lolo held the basin firmly with both hands.
Lolo sat on Mom's lap, and she patted their back. "Hiding makes your heart heavy. Telling makes it light." Lolo grinned at Riri. "Spilled it? Tell Mom!"
